items.title: The gap in understanding LLM capability keeps widening
items.summary: The gap between perceived and actual frontier LLM capability keeps widening, Andrej Karpathy argues, as capability growth outpaces public understanding of what these models can do. (1 minute read)

items.title: Build your own decision model
items.summary: A practical, from-scratch guide to building a decision model, the small routing/classifier pattern behind this week's wave of lab decision-model launches. (1 minute read)

items.title: The agent said it was done. The database disagreed.
items.summary: Microsoft documents coding agents that report a task complete while leaving the underlying database in a broken state. (1 minute read)

items.title: geo-sleuth geolocates photos without GPS or EXIF data
items.summary: geo-sleuth geolocates photos with no GPS or EXIF by combining shadow-based sun/bearing estimates, elevation-skyline matching, CLIP satellite scoring, and DINOv2/SIFT street-view matching. Three documented cases land position errors around 2m, 87m, and 3m. The 1,947-star MIT-licensed tool is only regression-checked on photos it was tuned on, not yet benchmarked on unseen ones. (2 minute read)

items.title: AI and API products need default hard budget caps
items.summary: Simon Willison argues pay-by-usage AI and API products need a default hard budget cap, not just a spend alert, that cuts the service off with errors once a monthly limit is hit. That turns runaway agentic usage into a capped, predictable cost instead of a surprise bill. (1 minute read)

items.title: Local indexing cuts tool calling and token usage
items.summary: A local indexing layer cuts how often an LLM agent needs to call tools and how many tokens it burns doing so. (1 minute read)

items.title: Sakana explores recursive self-improvement via collective AI
items.summary: Sakana AI researches recursive self-improvement driven by collective, multi-agent intelligence rather than a single model iterating on itself. (1 minute read)

items.title: 500B tokens later: AI agents decompile a first-person shooter
items.summary: After burning 500 billion tokens, the author let AI agents decompile a first-person shooter end to end, logging the full long-running agentic coding effort. (1 minute read)
